solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Peak amount of weight besetting one chap with tankard maybe (11)

indicatorNotes.besetting: to beset is to surround on all sides, so KILO goes round the rest

blocks.note: a kilo, a thousand grams
Roman numeral one
chap = man
a jar is a drinking vessel, and a jar of beer is a pint

annotation.surface: A mountaineer at the summit, weighed down by a companion clutching his beer mug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peak' looks like a high point of effort, but it is simply a mountain. 'Maybe' flags a tankard as just one example of a jar, a British word for a pint.
annotation.definitionFit: Kilimanjaro, in Tanzania, is Africa's highest peak.

entries.clue: Oxford college mostly keen to embrace British Library (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.to embrace: KEE wraps its arms around BL

blocks.note: KEEN 'mostly' drops its final N
standard abbreviation for the British Library

annotation.surface: An eager Oxford college keen to take over the British Library's collections.
annotation.walkthrough: KEE opens as KE…E to take BL.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Keble, founded in 1870 and named after the churchman John Keble, is one of Oxford University's colleges.

entries.clue: Student revised Keats and Poe — part of English Literature syllabus? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.revised: revising text changes it, so the letters of KEATS and POE are rearranged

blocks.note: L = learner, the student driver's plate
anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A student revising two poets for an English Literature exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revised' looks like exam study, which suits the student; here it rearranges letters. Keats was not himself a Lake Poet, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lake Poets, Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey, are a staple topic of English Literature courses.

entries.clue: Top cyclist Rick dismissing current in Mexico (6)

indicatorNotes.dismissing: sends a letter away from RICK
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so the shortened Rick sits inside Mexico's abbreviation

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current; take it out of RICK
abbreviation for Mexico

annotation.surface: A leading cyclist called Rick dropping out of a race in Mexico.
annotation.walkthrough: RCK sits inside MEX, splitting it as ME…X. 'Current' reads as a stream or trend but is the physics symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: Eddy Merckx, the Belgian five-time Tour de France winner, is often called the greatest cyclist ever.

entries.clue: Love characters regularly seen in Enfield (3)

indicatorNotes.characters regularly seen in: take letters at a regular interval: every second one

blocks.note: e N f I e L d: the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters

annotation.surface: Romance glimpsed now and then in a north London suburb.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks romantic but is the tennis score, zero. Enfield is a borough of north London.
annotation.definitionFit: Love means zero in tennis scoring, and nil is zero.

entries.clue: Strong drink curtailed all detective work (7)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: cut off at the tail, so ALL loses its last letter

blocks.note: ALL without its last L
cop = police officer
OP = opus, a work

annotation.surface: A hard-drinking detective whose investigation got cut short by the bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strong' is fair but a little cheeky: an alcopop is a sweet fizzy drink laced with alcohol.
annotation.definitionFit: An alcopop is an alcoholic soft drink, so a drink that is strong in the sense of containing alcohol.

entries.clue: Six deliveries, arranged under bed, taxed excessively (12)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters of UNDER BED are set in a new order

blocks.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A postman who has had to leave six parcels under someone's bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests the post; in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and six of them make an over.
annotation.definitionFit: Overburdened means loaded, or taxed, beyond what one can bear.

entries.clue: Iron withering piece of paper? (5,7)

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a withering remark is a cutting one

annotation.surface: A scorching iron shrivelling a sheet of paper.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the pun: the piece is cut from a paper, meaning a newspaper, not just a sheet.
annotation.definitionFit: A press cutting is an article clipped from a newspaper, literally a piece of a paper.

entries.clue: One who condemns beer drunk around our country run (7)

indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk thing is jumbled, so BEER's letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so the shuffled beer is wrapped round the country's letters

blocks.note: BEER 'drunk', rearranged
the setter is British: the United Kingdom
R = run, from cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A critic who deplores all the beer drunk across Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Our country' is the setter speaking: a British puzzle, so it means the United Kingdom. The run is tacked on after the container is built.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by derivation: to rebuke is to reprimand or censure, and the -er noun names the person doing it.

entries.clue: Enticement to obtain constant riches (5)

indicatorNotes.to obtain: LURE takes hold of C, containing it

blocks.note: a lure is a bait or enticement
c is the constant for the speed of light

annotation.surface: The eternal temptation of steady wealth.
annotation.walkthrough: LURE opens as LU…RE to hold C.
annotation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or riches, usually with a hint of disapproval.

entries.clue: That woman records family’s type of rug (9)

blocks.note: she = that woman
EPs are extended-play records
kin = family; the ’s reads as 'is', linking to the definition

annotation.surface: A woman's record collection laid out on the family's rug.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s on 'family’s' does double duty in the surface; in the parse it just says the family pieces make up the rug.
annotation.definitionFit: A sheepskin, the fleece with its hide, is a common rug.

entries.clue: Perhaps Titchmarsh in unusually sandy country once (9)

indicatorNotes.in: ALAN goes inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.unusually: SANDY is arranged in an unusual order

blocks.note: SANDY rearranged
Alan Titchmarsh, a British TV gardener; 'perhaps' because he is one Alan of many

annotation.surface: A celebrity gardener stuck in some unusually sandy foreign soil of the past.
annotation.walkthrough: Alan Titchmarsh is a well-known British gardening presenter, and 'perhaps' admits he is just one Alan. 'Sandy' looks like a description of the country, but it is the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Nyasaland was the British colonial name for what is now Malawi, so a country 'once'.

entries.clue: Some ibuprofen knocked back — after boozing here? (3)

indicatorNotes.Some: only part of the word is used
indicatorNotes.knocked back: the letters run backwards, as a drink is knocked back

blocks.note: the letters BUP sit inside iBUProfen

annotation.surface: Taking painkillers the morning after a night's drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests swallowing pills; it sends the hidden letters backwards. The definition is cryptic: the pub is where the boozing was done that calls for the ibuprofen.
annotation.definitionFit: A pub is where the boozing happens, and the question mark marks the playful definition.

entries.clue: Companion welcome to join unknown South American revolutionary (6)

blocks.note: CH = Companion of Honour, a British order
ave, Latin for hail, a welcome
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

annotation.surface: A comrade invited to join a mysterious Latin American rebel.
annotation.walkthrough: Hugo Chávez, the Venezuelan leader, styled himself a Bolivarian revolutionary.
annotation.definitionFit: Hugo Chávez led an attempted coup in Venezuela and later a self-proclaimed revolution as president.

entries.clue: Heard inheritor, Irishman, returning long-distance communication (7)

indicatorNotes.Heard: the word is to be taken by its sound
indicatorNotes.returning: coming back, so LIAM runs backwards

blocks.note: an inheritor is an heir, pronounced like 'air'
Liam, a typical Irish name

annotation.surface: An Irish heir sending word home from far away.
annotation.walkthrough: The silent H in HEIR is what makes it sound like AIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Airmail is post sent by aeroplane, typically over long distances.

entries.clue: German agreed with second agent about gemstone (6)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so REP runs backwards

blocks.note: ja is German for yes
s = second
a rep is a sales representative, an agent

annotation.surface: A German buyer striking a deal with a second dealer over a jewel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'German agreed' is one idea: the German word for agreement, JA.
annotation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, often red, semi-precious stone.

entries.clue: Question and answer primarily giving good advice for extinct creature (6)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: QU = question
A = answer
first letters of Giving Good Advice

annotation.surface: A question-and-answer session offering sound tips about a lost species.
annotation.walkthrough: The quagga is a rare word: a half-striped zebra of southern Africa, hunted out in the 1880s.
annotation.definitionFit: The quagga, a zebra subspecies, died out in the late 19th century.

entries.clue: Seaman’s thick black coat (3)

blocks.note: old slang for a sailor, from the days of tarred pigtails and canvas
the sticky black substance, from coal or wood, spread as a coating on roads and ropes

annotation.surface: A sailor's heavy dark jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: TAR is old slang for a sailor, as in Jack Tar. 'Coat' looks like clothing belonging to the seaman; it is a coating. The ’s reads as 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Tar is old slang for a sailor, and tar is the thick black stuff used to coat roads and ropes.

entries.clue: African pickle engrossing European person (9)

indicatorNotes.engrossing: to engross is to absorb, so SOUSE takes DANE inside

blocks.note: to souse is to pickle in brine or vinegar
a Dane, from Denmark

annotation.surface: An African in a pickle, absorbed by a European visitor.
annotation.walkthrough: SOUSE opens as SOU…SE to hold DANE. SOUDANESE is the old spelling of Sudanese.
annotation.definitionFit: Soudanese is an older spelling of Sudanese, a person from Sudan.

entries.clue: Duck and fish in centre of mere (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so the fish swims inside the middle of the mere
indicatorNotes.centre of: take the middle letters of MERE

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
the middle two letters of mERe

annotation.surface: Wildlife on a lake: a duck and a fish out in the middle of the water.
annotation.walkthrough: A mere is a small lake, which makes the scene; the ide is a freshwater fish worth knowing for crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its down.

entries.clue: Unfit, sleep briefly surrounded by relations (5)

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: to be surrounded by something is to have it on every side, so the short sleep is enclosed by the relations

blocks.note: to nap is to sleep for a short time
IT is a coy word for sex, as in sexual relations

annotation.surface: Someone too unwell to cope, dozing off while the relatives crowd round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family, but is the euphemism: IT means sexual relations.
annotation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or unfit for the purpose.

entries.clue: Group of workers book unwieldy boat (3)

blocks.note: TU = trade union
B = book

annotation.surface: A union booking a clumsy old boat for an outing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as a verb, to reserve; it is just the abbreviation B.
annotation.definitionFit: A disparaging sense: a slow, broad, awkward boat is mockingly called a tub, as if it were a bathtub afloat.

entries.clue: Doctor angered very important person (7)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A physician who has upset an important patient.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' sits at the front looking like a noun, the one who angered; it is a verb telling you to tamper with ANGERED.
annotation.definitionFit: A grandee is a person of high rank or eminence.

entries.clue: Part of body dance showing more happiness to Spooner (11)

indicatorNotes.to Spooner: as the Reverend Spooner would say it, swapping the opening sounds

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
gladder = happier
swap the B and GL sounds

annotation.surface: Dancing that lifts the spirits, and the body parts it works.
annotation.walkthrough: The Reverend Spooner is the crossword's patron of swapped initial sounds.
annotation.definitionFit: The gallbladder is the small organ below the liver that stores bile.
